user.title: Select sensors
user.description: Degree days are calculated from the long-term statistics of an outdoor temperature sensor. Optionally select a gas or energy meter to relate consumption to degree days.

data_description.temperature_sensor: Sensor measuring the outdoor temperature. It needs long-term statistics (state class measurement).
data_description.consumption_sensor: Optional gas or energy meter (state class total or total_increasing), e.g. the gas meter of a P1/DSMR reader or a heat pump energy sensor.

data_description.base_temperature: Reference indoor temperature. Degree days for a day = base temperature minus the mean outdoor temperature (18 °C in the Netherlands).
data_description.heating_limit: A day only counts when its mean outdoor temperature is below this limit (stookgrens). Usually equal to the base temperature.
data_description.weighting: Dutch weighting multiplies degree days by 1.1 (Nov-Feb), 1.0 (Mar, Oct) and 0.8 (Apr-Sep) to correct for solar gain, as used by Mindergas and Dutch energy suppliers.
data_description.baseline_usage: Consumption per day not related to heating (hot water, cooking), in the meter's unit. It is subtracted before calculating usage per degree day.
data_description.year_start_month: Month in which the yearly totals start, e.g. January for calendar years or July/August for heating seasons.
data_description.history_start: Oldest date read from the recorder statistics. Leave empty to read the last 10 years.
data_description.import_statistics: Store (weighted) degree days as long-term statistics so they can be shown and compared per day/week/month/year in the statistics graph card.

error.heating_limit_above_base: The heating limit cannot be higher than the base temperature.
